mech_interp_hum.title: Circuit Hermeneutics: Mechanistic Interpretability as Humanistic Inquiry
mech_interp_hum.info: by Owen Leonard, Fabian Offert, and Rita Raley (forthcoming in Cambridge Forum on AI: Culture and Society)
mech_interp_hum.desc: Our contribution to a forthcoming special issue of Cambridge Forum on AI on the "New Geometries of Language" will discuss the "mechanistic interpretability" approach to interpretive AI and the concerns it shares with humanistic textual analysis.

remediation_ocr_correction.title: Digitisation, Remediation, and the History of OCR Correction
remediation_ocr_correction.info: by Owen Leonard (forthcoming in Critical Approaches to Automated Text Recognition, ed. Melissa Terras, Paul Gooding, Sarah Ames and Joe Nockels)
remediation_ocr_correction.desc: My contribution to the Critical Approaches to Automated Text Recognition collection will present the history of OCR correction with attention to the further remediation that various techniques perform on already-remediated digitized texts.

infra_global_perception.title: The Global Perception Stack
infra_global_perception.info: by Owen Leonard (forthcoming in Cultural Politics of the Computational Image, ed. Paul Roquet)
infra_global_perception.desc: My contribution to the Cultural Politics of the Computational Image collection will examine the infrastructure underlying contemporary AI image generation through three case studies: Google's DeepDream, Nvidia's ThisPersonDoesNotExist, and OpenAI's DALL-E series of models.

berkeley_language_vision.title: Author(s) of Nature: The Media Politics of George Berkeley’s Language Analogy
berkeley_language_vision.desc: 'Author(s) of Nature' proposes to consider George Berkeley's "language analogy"—the idea, central to his philosophy, that the sensory world is structured like a language—in the political and media-technological context of Berkeley's Ireland.

stein_blind_glass.title: Through the Blind Glass: Combinatorial Hyperlangauge in Gertrude Stein's Tender Buttons
stein_blind_glass.desc: 'Through the Blind Glass' proposes to consider Stein's enigmatic 1914 book as 'hyperlanuage,' in which the legible sentence is merely an instance of an endlessly generative abstract schema.

morris_nm.title: ‘Object-Subject Terms’: Reading Robert Morris After the New Materialism
morris_nm.desc: "'Object-Subject Terms' explores the (possibly surprising) homologies between Robert Morris's critical writings of the late 1960s and the new materialism of the 2000s.

drama_life_dedalus.title: Drama, Life, and Stephen Dedalus: The Fate of Aestheticism in Joyce
drama_life_dedalus.desc: "Drama, Life, and Stephen Dedalus" traces Joyce's presentation of his literary surrogate from Stephen Hero to Ulysses, with particular attention to his tendency to see the world in aesthetic terms. Although the early Joyce takes this proclivity to be admirable, I show that it becomes a farce in A Portrait and a tragedy in Ulysses.
